# What the data-dict export loses: National Survey of Family Growth

The YAML files here follow data-dict spec 0.1.0. They describe the common data format, so they validate against its parquet files. The records in `metadata/` remain canonical. This table counts what the export drops or flattens into text.

| | `2022-2023` | `2017-2019` | `2015-2017` | `2013-2015` | `2011-2013` | `2006-2010` | `2002` | `1995` | `1988` | `1982` |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| variables exported | 83 | 75 | 38 | 42 | 42 | 44 | 43 | 20 | 20 | 20 |
| variables whose numeric code labels went to `details` (no labeled numeric codes) | 68 | 59 | 28 | 25 | 25 | 28 | 27 | 12 | 16 | 14 |
| missing or unresolved codes, typed only in the `__code` column's labels | 69 | 47 | 28 | 47 | 23 | 53 | 37 | 18 | 16 | 24 |
| variables with several wordings, flattened into `details` | 4 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| availability entries (wave by form, with n), summarized as one line of text | 83 | 75 | 38 | 42 | 42 | 44 | 43 | 20 | 20 | 20 |
| corrections applied; only the corrected text is exported | 1 | 0 | 7 | 11 | 11 | 2 | 1 | 6 | 2 | 7 |
| field origins (publisher, data file, rule, hand, model) not exported | 521 | 541 | 246 | 275 | 275 | 286 | 279 | 129 | 129 | 131 |
